recap.workouts:
Two sessions, both exactly as called, and the one that mattered produced a real number.

06:00 Rainbow — taken at its absolute lightest, and the file proves it: 52 min in the gym, avg HR 104, max 140, training load 13, RPE 3. Your note: done very easy, feel alright. The biggest collision on this week's calendar, defused completely — you arrived at the run on legs that had done essentially nothing.

RT19 — RUN TUNE. 90 min, 16.96 km, load 101 against a planned 104 (97.1% compliance, paired cleanly to the planned session). Avg HR 152, max 173, RPE 6. Your note: executed perfectly.

Warm-up 5' at 5:47/km, HR 120. Z2 lead-in 10.7' at 5:09/km, HR 141.

The 20' block (prescribed 4:20-4:40/km, HR-governed). Five-minute splits: 4:16 · 4:38 · 4:26 · 4:30, with HR 159 · 162 · 163 · 167. You went out marginally quick, made ONE correction inside the first eight minutes — exactly what the execution rule asked for — then locked 4:26-4:30 and never touched it again. Block total 19.6' at 4:27/km. Settled-start to end HR drift +4.0 bpm, decoupling 2.8%, smoothed steadiness 3.8% CV — as steady as the indoor CT31 block, and that on rolling terrain at 1850-1919 m. Last five minutes: 4:30/km at a 167 plateau, max 173. HR never ran away and pace never sagged. That is a block AT threshold, not above it — exactly what you reported when you said you could have held it about an hour.

The 50' Z2 tail: 5:30/km, dead centre of the 5:01-5:45 band, ten-minute reads 5:36 · 5:28 · 5:29 · 5:31 · 5:27 — flat as a ruler across 80 m of climbing. HR averaged 154 against a Z2 ceiling of 150, so about four beats warm: 152 · 156 · 157 · 154 · 151, lifting into the climbs and settling again each time. Decoupling across the tail was -0.7%, meaning speed per beat was very slightly BETTER in the second half than the first. That is an honest Z2 tail on tired legs after a threshold block, not a victory lap at Zone X. Cool-down 5' at 5:48.
recap.takeaways:
1) The tune: your run anchors are now MEASURED, not borrowed. Run LTHR 162 -> 167 and threshold pace 4:20 -> 4:22/km, medium confidence. The 162 was never yours — it was copied off your bike LTHR on 7 July and has been sitting in the file ever since. 167 lands +8 above bike LTHR 159, the normal run-versus-bike offset, so the analyzer established it rather than misreading it as threshold falling. Run VO2max estimate 55.9 -> 55.5, i.e. a 2 s/km pace change: noise, not a decline. FTP 236 W and bike LTHR 159 are untouched — RT19 says nothing about the bike.

2) On this morning's call, straight: I recommended sliding this to Friday and you ran it anyway. The data says you read your body better than I read the panel — plateau right at threshold, +4 bpm drift, 2.8% decoupling, 97% compliance. I own that. It does not cancel the readiness signal (sleeping HR up four mornings running, temp flagged twice, Form -21) — it means the signal did not cash out today. Keep watching it; don't now decide it was nothing.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RT19 EXECUTED, Rainbow executed at its lightest as prescribed, no lifting scheduled Thursday. Nothing in the remaining week moves.

4) The week's actual deliverable is done. Both tunes are banked — bike Tuesday, run today — and Week 9 gets built on numbers you measured rather than placeholders. Friday and Saturday are toppers now, not requirements.

recovery.bannerSub: Lowest readiness of the whole block. Sleeping HR is now up a fifth straight morning and breathing has joined it, while Form sits at −25.8, the deepest of the block. Both tunes are already banked, so today's run is a topper with nothing to prove — the class stays light and RAn4 comes off.
recovery.note: Gmail export in at 05:29, on time — and one honest caveat first: the watch stopped recording at 02:34, mid-REM, with no wake segment, so last night's file shows 5h29 asleep from a 20:49 start. That is a truncated record, not proof of a short night, and I am not going to treat it as one; it costs the index only about two points anyway. The call rests on the two signals that ARE clean. Sleeping HR came in at 64 avg / 54 min for the fifth straight elevated morning (58 → 61 → 63 → 64 → 64), pushing the 3-night smooth to 63.7 against a 57.3 baseline, z −2.1, the widest gap of the block. Respiratory rate has now formally joined it: 14.3 last night, smooth 13.9 vs a 13.4 baseline, z −1.4, which trips the elevated-breathing flag for the first time. Readiness lands at 27 / Ease off — the lowest reading in the 21-day series. Form is −25.8 (CTL 49.3 − ATL 75.1), deeper again after RT19's load of 101. One genuinely good piece of news, and credit where it is due: wrist temp fell to 35.4 and the temperature flag has CLEARED — your explanation yesterday (bedroom a degree warmer, later dinner) was right and my read of it was the more alarmist one. So here is the clear recommendation: take Cutthroat at [FITNESS] with a light bar and smooth singles, let the class accessory be your entire Friday arm dose, and CUT RAn4 today. This is not yesterday repeating itself — yesterday a real deliverable was on the line and you were right to run it; today there is no deliverable at all. Both tunes are banked, RAn4 is the plan's own designated first cut, and ten minutes of Z4 running buys nothing that the next block will not buy better from a body that actually absorbed this week. The failure mode I care about is a deload that does not deload; that is what turns week 9 into week 4 again. If you want to keep something, keep Saturday's CAn4 and decide it on Saturday's numbers.
